To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
T cell activation is necessary for Ag-induced eotaxin expression and pulmonary eosinophilia in an in vivo model of allergic asthma.
T cell-dependent regulation of eosinophila in the lung is associated with the induction and regulation of the eosinophil chemokine, eotaxin.
(1) eotaxin expression in the lung is dependent on the activation of Ag-specific T lymphocytes, and (2) eotaxins are likely involved in the Ag-specific recruitment of eosinophil into the lung.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular mechanisms of T cell-dependent eosino-philia and its role in allergic asthma.
the mechanisms of T cell-dependent regulation of chemokines and eosinophil recruitment in the lung.
the regulation of eosinophil recruitment into the lung by T cell activation in an allergic mouse model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

T cells are involved in the regulation of pulmonary eosinophilia in an Ag-specific manner and that the eosinophil chemoattractant eotaxin may play an important role in the recruitment of these cells into the lung.
T cell-dependent eosino-philia in a mouse model of pulmonary eosinophilia involves eotaxin expression in the lung.
T cells play a role in the recruitment of inflammatory cells to the lung, and this role can be mediated by chemokine induction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ag-specific T cell activation is necessary for the expression of eoxin and the recruitment of the eosinophils, and that the eosinophila is independent of mast cell activation.
the T cell-dependent regulation of chemokines is an important mechanism by which the T cell regulates eosinophil recruitment in the lung in vivo.
the induction of eotoxin is a T cell-dependent process, and that eotaxine is an important eosinophil chemoattractant that mediates Ag-induced pulmonary eosnophila.
The main takeaway from our work is that
T cells are necessary for eosinophilia and that T cell-derived cytokines, particularly eotaxin are involved in eosinophil recruitment.
T cell-dependent recruitment of eosinophil into the lung in this model is mediated by eotaxin expression, and not by mast cell degranulating or Ag-specific antibody responses.
T lymphocytes play an essential role in regulating eotaxin expression, and thereby mediate the recruitment of eosino-phils to the lung.
